dispatcher.name: Delegate
dispatcher.desc: Every request starts here. Delegate picks a trigger, gathers its items, gives each a repeatable workflow ID, and sends new ones on to the workflow that fits. It never does the checking itself.

steps.what: Picks the trigger for the request

why.label: What to run
why.sum: Works out what to run: your triggers (tick boxes, a named list, or all), one trigger, one workflow on one item, a test, a rerun, several items in turn, or changing items by hand (skip, mark, delete, the Run each item once switch). Any trigger run can be “pull in only”. Nothing matches: says so and lists what can run.

alts.then: Reruns that run as a new attempt

alts.when: Says run workflow manager, or names triggers
alts.then: Tick boxes, or the named triggers; each runs as above

alts.when: Says skip, mark or delete wf-…, or turns Run each item once on or off
alts.then: Changes them by hand in the done list, or the switch; runs nothing

steps.title: Pick the trigger
Run that item again
steps.what: Looks up the workflow ID and sends the same item to its workflow as the next attempt

why.label: Rerun a workflow
why.sum: A rerun is a new attempt of the same run, never a new workflow.

simulated.label: If: you ask to rerun a run

res.d1: Names a workflow ID, so it's a rerun

out: Starts the next attempt of that run

workflows.name: Change a skill
workflows.desc: Creating, editing, renaming or deleting a skill, or doing what an Ask-mode answer offered. Each edit is a draft: the architect keeps the Workflow Viewer in step with it, shows it beside the chat and stops, so you can try it and change more. The checks, the impact review and the save wait for Publish.

steps.what: Reads the rules and names the skill's role

why.label: Change mode · step 1
why.sum: The project says to consult the architect before touching .claude/skills/.

steps.title: Read the rules
steps.tip: Read the design rules and decide what job this skill does.

steps.what: Makes the change and redraws its picture

why.label: Change mode · steps 2 and 3
why.sum: Rewrites any step the change makes wrong. Never patches with “skip this”.

steps.title: Make the change
steps.tip: Make the requested change to the skill and redraw its diagram.

steps.what: Updates the Workflow Viewer's definition to match the skill

why.label: Change mode · step 4
why.sum: If the skill is shown on the Workflow Viewer, its steps, branches, quotes and tests there are changed to match.

steps.title: Match the Workflow Viewer
steps.tip: Update the board's picture of the workflow to match the change.

steps.title: Quick build of the board
steps.what: Rebuilds the board so it shows the draft; any errors are listed to fix before publishing, never a stop

why.label: Change mode · step 5
why.sum: A draft is shown straight away; the heavy checks wait for Publish (rule 27).

steps.tip: Rebuild the board so it shows the draft, listing any problems.

steps.title: Show the board beside the chat
steps.what: Opens the workflow's page in the browser pane on the first edit, and reloads it after each later one

why.label: Change mode · step 6
why.sum: You see the draft on the board while you work on it.

steps.tip: Open the workflow's page beside the chat, or refresh it.

steps.title: Say it's a draft
steps.what: Says what changed and that it's a draft: try it, change more, or say publish

why.label: Change mode · step 7
why.sum: No checks, no review and no save on a draft: those run once, when you publish.

steps.tip: Tell you what changed and that it's only a draft so far.

res.a10: Draft: try it, or say publish

res.a4: Every board definition that names it updated
res.a8: Built: 1 error listed to fix before publishing
res.a10: Draft, with the error to fix

workflows.name: Publish a draft
workflows.desc: Making a draft the current version, when you say “publish workflow …”, “save a version” or press Publish on the board. The heavy part runs once: the checks, the draft checked against earlier runs and shown on the board, your approval of anything that will no longer happen, then one version with a note in plain words.

steps.title: Gather the draft and its runs
steps.what: One call: the board build's problems, the draft's changes in plain words, the diff and the earlier runs to check it against

why.label: Publish mode · step 1
why.sum: Everything the heavy part needs, gathered once.

steps.tip: Collect the draft's changes and the earlier runs to compare against.

steps.title: Run the checks
steps.what: Runs the checks on the draft and any skill it could affect

why.label: Publish mode · step 2
why.sum: Doesn't publish while a check fails.

alts.then: Fixes the draft, then gathers it again

steps.tip: Does the draft pass every check, for itself and related skills?

steps.title: Check it against earlier runs
steps.what: Judges each earlier run: same, might change or will change, with a reason; shows the review under History › Draft on the board

why.label: Publish mode · step 3
why.sum: You can open each run that may change on the flow before anything is saved (rule 27).

steps.tip: Work out which earlier runs would turn out differently with this draft.

steps.title: Your approval
steps.what: Goes on by itself when nothing stops happening; otherwise the bar lists what will no longer happen and you approve it in the chat

why.label: Publish mode · step 4
why.sum: Anything the draft will no longer do is saved only once you have approved it.

alts.then: Stops; the draft and its review stay on the board

steps.tip: Do you accept what the workflow will no longer do?

steps.title: Save it as one version
steps.what: Saves the draft to the workflow's history with a note in plain words and its review, so it shows under History and can be put back later

why.label: Publish mode · step 5
why.sum: One publish is one version, saved with what the workflow now does differently and its review (rule 27).

steps.tip: Save the draft as a new version you can go back to.

res.p4: Only what you asked: no extra yes
res.p5: Saved as v3 with the review

res.p3: 1 run might change: shown on the board
2 runs will change: shown on the board

workflows.name: Ask how to change the setup
workflows.desc: You ask how to add or change something, e.g. a new trigger. The architect says the one or two things it needs, draws you the planned design, and builds it only after you say yes.

steps.title: Find the common request
steps.what: Looks the request up in the Common requests table

why.label: Ask mode · steps 1 and 2
why.sum: Known requests have a ready short answer; new ones get a row.

steps.tip: Match your question to a kind of request already known.

steps.title: Details already given?
steps.what: Checks you've said what the request needs (e.g. source, triggers, what to do)

why.label: Ask mode · step 1 + Common requests

steps.tip: Have you given everything needed to plan this, or is something missing?

steps.title: Show the planned design

workflows.name: Debug a skill
workflows.desc: A skill doesn't trigger, or the wrong one is chosen. The architect checks the likely causes in order and stops at the first one it finds.

steps.what: Checks the skill is loaded and its header is right

why.label: Debug mode · causes 1 and 2
why.sum: Stops at the first cause found: wrong place or folder, or a broken name/description header.

steps.title: Loaded, header OK?
steps.tip: Is the skill installed in the right place and set up properly?

steps.what: Checks its description is clear and not shared with another skill

why.label: Debug mode · causes 3 and 4
why.sum: A vague description, or one that covers another skill's job, makes the wrong skill get picked.

steps.title: Description clear?
steps.tip: Does the skill's description clearly say its job, without overlapping another?

steps.what: Checks for old skill names and broken rules

why.label: Debug mode · causes 5 and 6
why.sum: Looks for a renamed or deleted skill still named somewhere, then runs the checks.

steps.title: Old names or broken rules?
steps.tip: Are outdated skill names or broken design rules causing the problem?

steps.what: Reports the cause and the smallest fix

why.label: Debug mode · report
why.sum: Says what was wrong and the smallest change that fixes it.

steps.title: Cause and smallest fix
steps.tip: Explain what went wrong and the smallest change that fixes it.

res.b3: Not reached: stopped at the first cause
res.b4: Cause: weak description. Fix: add “check my emails” style phrases
